studies.officialTitle: A Phase 3 Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of HRS-7535 Tablets in Subjects With Overweight or Obesity

design.description: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial evaluating once-daily oral HRS-7535 at 120 mg and 180 mg versus placebo (2:2:1 randomization) for 44 weeks, continuing through Week 50, in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18 years or older with overweight or obesity (mean baseline body weight 94.1 kg, mean baseline BMI 34.0 kg/m2, 62% female), without diabetes.
studies.overallDuration: 44 weeks of randomized treatment, continuing through Week 50
studies.safetySummary: Most treatment-emergent adverse events were mild to moderate and gastrointestinal-related. Common TEAEs with HRS-7535 (120 mg and 180 mg, respectively) were nausea (70.3% and 70.0% vs 16.2% placebo), vomiting (66.7% and 68.6% vs 4.5% placebo), and diarrhea (36.9% and 35.9% vs 15.3% placebo). Treatment discontinuations due to TEAEs were 4.1% (120 mg) and 3.1% (180 mg) vs 2.7% (placebo). No liver safety signals were observed.

studies.officialTitle: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blinded, Placebo-controlled, Parallel-group Phase ⅡStudy to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of HRS-7535 in Obese Subjects

design.description: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial conducted at 29 centers in China evaluating once-daily oral HRS-7535 at target doses of 30 mg, 60 mg, 120 mg, and 180 mg versus placebo (1:1:1:1:1) over 26 weeks, continuing through Week 36, in adults with obesity without diabetes.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18 to 75 years with obesity (BMI 28.0 to 40.0 kg/m2) without type 2 diabetes.
studies.overallDuration: 26 weeks of primary treatment, continuing through Week 36
studies.safetySummary: Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 93.5%-97.9% of participants receiving HRS-7535 versus 91.3% with placebo, predominantly mild to moderate gastrointestinal events during dose escalation. Nausea (16.7%-58.3% vs 4.3%), vomiting (18.8%-43.8% vs 2.2%), and diarrhea (18.8%-26.1% vs 8.7%) were the most common. Serious AEs occurred in 1 (2.1%), 2 (4.3%), 0 (0%), and 3 (6.3%) receiving 30, 60, 120, and 180 mg, versus 1 (2.2%) with placebo. Discontinuations due to AEs occurred in 1 (2.1%), 1 (2.1%), 0 (0%), and 3 (6.3%) versus 0 with placebo. One death occurred in the 30 mg group (unrelated sudden death). No liver function abnormalities or acute pancreatitis occurred.

design.description: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo parallel-controlled Phase 1b/2 clinical study evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of multiple escalating doses of once-daily oral HRS-7535 tablets versus placebo over 24 weeks in obese subjects.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18 to 65 years with overweight or obesity.

studies.officialTitle: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Phase II Clinical Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of HRS-7535 in Subjects With Heart Failure, Mild Reduction/Preservation of Ejection Fraction, and Obesity

design.description: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 clinical study evaluating the efficacy and safety of once-daily oral HRS-7535 versus placebo over 36 weeks in participants with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF) and obesity.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18 years or older with heart failure (HFmrEF or HFpEF, LVEF >= 40%) and obesity (BMI >= 28 kg/m2).
